role.altitude: The chemical engineer keeps deciding controls, inspecting equipment, diagnosing causes and finding improvements; looking up hazard data, exporting trends into spreadsheets, checking values against limits by eye and routing documents for signature shrink.
skills_to_grow: Setting control limits and permit rules
Editing drafted procedures against the hazard register
role.ambitious_version: An engineer who sees deviations as they happen and spends the time on causes and improvements.

tasks.short: Review hazards, decide controls, write safety procedures for workers operating equipment or working near chemical reactions, review them with operators and safety staff, and route them for approval and release.

steps.what: Engineer reviews hazards from the risk assessment, safety data sheets and incident history
Engineer decides controls and safe working steps for the chemical reactions and equipment
Engineer writes the safety procedures

loop.input: The engineer's controls and step notes, the hazard register and the procedure template.
loop.output: A draft procedure with standard sections filled and step text written.
loop.check: Every hazard and control in the text must exist in the register or the engineer's notes, and any extra is removed; the engineer checks that each step tells the worker what to do, in the right order and with the control decided for it, and edits each step.
loop.stop: The engineer writes the steps by hand when the draft misses a hazard.
loop.why_not_simpler: Step wording differs per unit and reaction.

steps.what: Engineer reviews the draft with operators and safety staff
Engineer routes the procedure for approval signatures and chases them: on paper today, in the document control system after the change
Engineer checks the final signed procedure: steps, controls, signatures and the equipment and area it applies to
Engineer releases the checked procedure in the document control system

tasks.design: The procedure template pulls hazards, protective equipment and permit needs from the risk register and the safety data sheet database for the equipment and chemicals involved, instead of the engineer looking each up. Deciding the controls stays with the engineer. A drafting step writes step text from the engineer's notes, with every hazard and control traceable to the register, and the engineer edits each step. After review with operators, the document control system routes the procedure for approval signatures instead of paper routing; the engineer checks the signed version and releases it.

approvals.approved_version: The safety procedure with its steps, controls and signatures exactly as checked by the engineer in s5b, released once in the document control system for the named equipment and area; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Hazard data were looked up by hand and procedures routed on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Hazard registers linked to templates and document control workflows.
tasks.still_hard: Novel reactions with little hazard data.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the shortcut operators will take and closing it.
tasks.altitude: Less looking up and routing; deciding controls stays.

reach.learn: Whether procedures are clearer and released sooner.

evidence.claim: In a writing experiment with 453 professionals, not engineers, a model cut time by 40% and raised quality by 18%.
The signing engineer stays responsible for procedures.

assumptions: Boundary: developing safety procedures; directing workers (task 3555) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: risk register and safety data sheet database kept by safety staff, covering about 70% of equipment and chemicals; s1 is priced at that share.
Deciding controls and reviewing with operators keep their full time.
s3 keeps 70: step text is drafted from the engineer's notes, but each step is edited for the workers who use it.
unknowns: Number of procedures written or revised per year.
research_questions: Are procedures released sooner without more review comments?

incremental.description: Engineer keeps the procedure template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: novel processes outside the register, so hazards are still looked up (s1 keeps 85) and procedures mostly written by hand (s3 keeps 85) (12.7); high: many similar procedures on known equipment (19.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Pull process data around the event, inspect equipment and talk with operators, diagnose the cause of problems with chemical manufacturing processes, decide the fix, and record the problem.

steps.what: Engineer gathers trends, alarms, lab results and shift notes around the problem
Engineer inspects the equipment and talks with operators
Engineer diagnoses the cause of the problems with the manufacturing processes
Engineer decides and directs the fix
Engineer records the problem, cause and fix

tasks.design: An event view in the process historian shows trends, alarms, lab results and shift notes for the chosen unit and time window, instead of the engineer exporting each to spreadsheets. Inspecting, diagnosing and deciding the fix stay with the engineer. The problem record is a form linked to the event view, so the data need not be pasted in, and past problems can be searched by unit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data for each problem were exported and lined up by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Historian event views linked to lab and shift systems.
tasks.still_hard: Problems from raw material changes not in any system.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a pump that sounds wrong.

evidence.claim: Test data and root cause work suit dashboards and statistics, with a model at most clustering free-text reports.

assumptions: Boundary: troubleshooting problems; testing and monitoring control over variables (task 18473) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: lab results and shift notes stored electronically, for about 70% of units; s1 is priced at that share.
Shift notes are used for the event, not to judge operators.
Inspecting, diagnosing and deciding keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of problems investigated per month.
research_questions: Does time from problem to fix fall?

incremental.description: Engineer maintains event view templates per unit.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: units with paper logs and lab sheets, so data are still gathered by hand and s1 keeps 80 (7.7); high: about 70% of units with electronic data as assumed (15.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect process and lab data, review trends against targets, analyze causes of deviations and experiment results, and share findings with the team.

steps.what: Engineer collects process and lab data from processes and experiments into spreadsheets
Engineer reviews trends against targets and limits
Engineer analyzes causes of deviations and experiment results
Engineer shares findings with operators and the team

tasks.design: A dashboard on the process historian and the lab system shows each unit's key variables and experiment results, instead of the engineer exporting them to spreadsheets each day. Control charts flag points outside limits and runs of points drifting, so the engineer reviews flags and trends instead of scanning every series. Analysing causes and sharing findings stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were exported to spreadsheets every day.
tasks.still_hard: Experiments run outside the lab system.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which drift matters for product quality.

ambition.what: Review each shift instead of each day.

reach.learn: Whether drifts are caught a shift earlier.

evidence.claim: Test data and root cause work suit dashboards and statistics; recurring status reports become a dashboard.

assumptions: Boundary: monitoring and analysing data; tests of degree of control over variables (task 18473) and progress reports for management (task 3554) are sibling tasks.
s2 covers the daily trend review; formal capability studies are counted in task 18473.
Input contract for s1: lab results flow from the lab system, for about 80% of tests; s1 is priced at that share.
Analysing and sharing keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of variables reviewed per day.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many experiments outside the lab system, so data are still exported (s1 keeps 60) and series scanned by hand (s2 keeps 80) (14.5); high: connected units and lab as designed (27.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather performance and emission data, check compliance with safety and environmental regulations, inspect equipment, identify ways to optimize performance, and write the evaluation.

steps.what: Engineer gathers performance data: yields, energy use, emissions and equipment efficiency
Engineer checks measured values against permit limits and safety and environmental regulations
Engineer inspects the chemical equipment on site
Engineer identifies ways to optimize performance and judges compliance gaps
Engineer writes the evaluation with recommendations

tasks.design: A dashboard on the historian, energy meters and emission monitoring shows yields, energy use, emissions and equipment efficiency per unit, instead of the engineer compiling them. Coded rules compare measured values with permit limits and operating constraints and flag exceedances and near misses for the engineer to review. Inspecting equipment and finding improvements stay with the engineer; the evaluation template places the tables.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were compiled by hand and checked against permits line by line.
tasks.enabler_now: Plant dashboards and coded permit rules.
tasks.still_hard: Permit conditions written as open text.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which improvement the plant can actually run.
tasks.altitude: Less compiling and checking; judgement stays.

reach.learn: Whether near misses are seen before they become exceedances.

evidence.claim: An industrial design assistant flags violations of parameters, regulations and constraints.

assumptions: Boundary: evaluating equipment and processes; production cost estimates (task 3554) and equipment layout (task 3560) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: permit limits coded as rules once by the environment officer, covering about 70% of conditions; s2 is priced at that share.
Inspecting and identifying improvements keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of permit conditions that are numeric.
research_questions: Do near misses get acted on before exceedances?

incremental.description: Engineer updates permit rules after permit changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: open-text permit conditions the rules cannot code, so s2 keeps 80, and meters not connected, so s1 keeps 70 (14.0); high: numeric permit limits and connected meters (25.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
